learning_outcomes.text: The students will be able to independently use Matlab/Simulink programming environment to solve specific technical problems, especially in matrix calculus, to develop their own functions and m-files and Simulink simulations.
This knowledge can be largely used in related technical courses.

syllabus_topics: Matlab Desktop, help, command window, workspace window, command history window, Array editor window
Matlab basic, arithmetic operation, Matlab operators, complex numbers, Matlab functions
Array and array operations, Matlab functions
Data types (import, export, work with data)
Statistical data analysis, polynomial, data interpolation
Transfer data between Simulink and Matlab

assessment_methods.method: Practical part semestral project (a program developed in Matlab with the student's own graphic environment)

assessment_rules: The course is ended by an examination composed of two parts: 2 tests (approx. in weeks 6-7 and 13) - programming simple mathematical tasks, and a practical part semestral project (a program developed in Matlab with the student's own graphic environment).
bibliography: Bruce Littlefield. Mastering MATLAB. Prentice Hall, 2005.
James B. Dabney, Thomas L. Harman. Mastering Simulink. Prentice Hall, 2004.
degree: Bachelor's programme, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Informatics - courses in English
